text:
ana: quick sync — proposing an RBAC tweak and workflow updates for the scan-runner service account (the job that runs SAST/DAST during CI). this touches KMS-wrapped build artifacts, pre-merge gating, and incident rollback if a scan blocks deploys.
ben: can you outline the minimal perms? do we need decrypt or just read metadata from the artifact store? :thinking_face:
ana: minimal: list/read artifact metadata only. no KMS decrypt on CI — instead we want the scanner to fetch an ephemeral, KMS-unwrapped copy produced by the builder step. the service acct currently has broader storage and kms:decrypt perms we want to narrow.
olivia: adding SAST/triage notes — last time we tightened perms we saw a flurry of false positives because the scanner couldn't fetch symbol tables. we need a mitigation plan to avoid blocking merges.
security-bot: FYI: recent SAST run flagged repo redwood/platform at tools/packager.py:124 rule 'missing-sanitizer'. full scan id: scans/2331. retention: KMS audit logs 90 days.
devex: pipeline plan:
  1) pre-merge gate keeps SAST as a warning for 48h while we roll out RBAC changes to avoid mass-blocks.
  2) add a conditional enforcement step: if PR has label `sast-enforce`, gate applies; otherwise it's advisory.
  3) require PRs that change scanner or build auth to include a triage ticket with 'artifact smoke' evidence (logs showing scanner fetched required files).
oncall: rollback / incident playbook if scanner fails and blocks release:
  - immediate: flip the gate to advisory, revert RBAC change if deployed to prod, open incident INC-5509.
  - gather: KMS audit logs for service acct for last 1h, build artifact access logs, and SAST report bundle.
  - owners: @ben (rollback exec), @ana (postmortem and remediation).
sre: DAST considerations: our DAST probe for staging uses dynamic payloads and needs network access to telemetry buckets. recommend the RBAC change include an allowlist for staging-only indices and a short TTL on tokens.
ben: how do we query KMS audit for the service account quickly? can you paste the gcloud example we should attach to PRs?
ana: sure — example KMS + storage audit queries to run after canary RBAC roll:

```
# KMS key access by service account in last 60m
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"scanner-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com\" AND protoPayload.methodName:\"google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt\"" --limit 50 --project=redwood-prod

# Storage object reads by scanner service acct
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail=\"scanner-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com\" AND protoPayload.methodName:\"storage.objects.get\"" --limit 200 --project=redwood-prod
```

olivia: triage workflow for flagged findings in this rollout:
  - if scan produces >50 high/critical findings across multiple PRs, pause enforcement and open a triage umbrella ticket (TRI-1222).
  - maintain a suppression registry entry only if patch + tests committed in the same PR and a reviewer from security signs off.
  - require unit/e2e evidence attached to suppression requests.
devex: I'll add a PR checklist template: `RBAC diff, KMS audit snippet, scanner smoke logs, triage ticket link, suppression form if used` and make SAST advisory by default for 48h.
oncall: monitoring rules: alert if scanner error rate >5% after RBAC change or if any audit log shows kms.decrypt called by scanner-sa. escalation to SEC-ONCALL.
sre: recommend a short-lived feature flag that forces scanner to fall back to cached artifacts if it can't fetch remote ones. reduces blast radius while we tighten perms.
ben: ok i'm comfortable with the staged approach. i'll run the canary RBAC change in dev and post audit outputs here. ETA 3h.
ana: thanks — follow-ups: devex will add PR template, olivia will prepare suppression review checklist, ben runs canary + shares KMS logs, oncall will prepare INC-5509 runbook, sre will add fallback flag to scanner.
security-bot: Reminder: attach the KMS audit export and the advisory-to-enforce timeline to the PR. KMS audit retention: 90 days.
